parole.testo: From Middle High German arche, byform of more common arke, from Old High German arka, archa, from Proto-Germanic *arkō, from Latin arca. The expected German form is Arke. The ch-form is native in parts of Upper German. It was reinforced in the modern standard language by the Medieval Latin spelling

From Middle High German ebene, from Old High German ebanī, noun form of eban (“even”) from Proto-Germanic *ebnaz. By surface analysis, eben (“even”) + -e. The sense “plane” is a semantic loan from Latin planum, whereas the sense “storey, floor” is one from English level.

parole.significato: a rack of shelves, shelving, a shelf (in this collective sense), e.g. an open bookcase
parole.testo: Early 17th century, of unclear origin. Hypotheses include: * Derived from Proto-Germanic *rigǭ ~ *rīgǭ ~ *rīhǭ, whence German Riege and Reihe (both originally “row, line”). * Derived from Latin rēgula, whence German Riegel (“bar, latch”), Dutch richel (“bar, latch”, dialectally also “rack”).
